basis: Inherited coagulation defect; cerebral hemorrhage and joint/intramuscular hemorrhage each occur in 30-79%, supporting brain and musculoskeletal injury.
Combined immunodeficiency; thrombocytopenia in 4/4 and anemia in 2/4 support blood involvement. Recurrent infections and diarrhea alone do not establish structural organ injury.
Central motor control disorder causing dystonia; muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease. Contractures reported in one patient do not establish common involvement.
Inherited erythroid marrow hypoplasia causing macrocytic anemia; no additional organ damage established at >=30%.
Progressive skeletal muscular dystrophy with frequently associated cardiomyopathy in its definition. Respiratory muscle impairment belongs to the muscular disease.
Atherosclerotic thrombotic occlusion of the distal abdominal aorta; claudication alone does not establish skeletal muscle injury.
Inherited pentose phosphate pathway enzyme deficiency associated with hemolytic anemia; metabolic and red-cell disease.
Congenital retinal signaling disorder causing stationary visual impairment; broad nervous-system ancestry does not imply brain disease.
Hereditary corticospinal tract disease; additional organ manifestations vary among subtypes and are not established across most of the umbrella.
Defined as carcinoma arising in cutaneous apocrine sweat glands, occupying dermis and subcutaneous tissue.
Inherited retinal dystrophy defined by retinal degeneration and visual loss.
Hereditary glioma susceptibility assigned to its specified CNS tumor site; predisposition does not establish an existing tumor or additional organ damage.
Malignancy of B-lineage lymphoid blood cells; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis. No common extranodal site specified.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia; fixed lower-limb contractures occur in 80-99% and muscle atrophy in 8/10. Optic atrophy is only 5-29%; nystagmus alone is not eye damage.
Defining triad of pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, nephropathy and sensorineural deafness; each documented in 3/3 patients.
Primary neurologic headache disorder; no additional organ injury is intrinsic to migraine without aura.
Complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy defined by kidney injury, hemolysis and thrombocytopenia. Secondary hypertension does not establish additional direct organ injury.
Renal hamartomas/nephroblastomatosis and pancreatic islet hypertrophy define the syndrome; developmental impairment in 80-99%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver dysfunction.
Toxic or nutritional damage to the optic nerve, which belongs to the ocular axis; immune causation is not established by the optic-neuritis parent.
Renal tubular disease with phosphate wasting/acidosis; rickets in 19/19 supports bone involvement. Emphysema in 3/12 is below 30%; hypertension is secondary.
Defined by disease of the cerebral cortex; no additional organ involvement applies across the umbrella.
Vitamin D signaling resistance with defective skeletal mineralization and rickets. Alopecia occurs in only 5-29%.
Heme synthesis disorder with phototoxic cutaneous disease in 3/3. Iron deficiency anemia in 1/3 is a separately diagnosed condition; common hepatic injury is not established.
Malignant tumor occupying the supratentorial brain; visual field deficits from cerebral lesions do not establish ocular disease.
Malignant astrocytic glioma arising in the central nervous system; no additional commonly damaged organ specified.
